subsystems.name: Detection medium
subsystems.role: the vast, transparent volume where a neutrino occasionally interacts and makes a flash of light.
parts: purified water or liquid scintillator in an underground tank (Super-Kamiokande, KamLAND, Borexino)

subsystems.name: Optical sensors
subsystems.role: catch the faint Cherenkov light and convert it to electrical pulses.

subsystems.name: Deployment infrastructure
subsystems.role: gets sensors kilometres down into ice or water and keeps them there.

subsystems.name: Data, timing and triggering
subsystems.role: turns nanosecond photon hits into events with a direction.
parts: data links to the surface or shore station

subsystems.name: Calibration and background rejection
subsystems.role: separates rare neutrino events from the far more numerous cosmic-ray muons.

subsystems.name: Reconstruction and analysis
subsystems.role: fits photon arrival times to a direction and energy, then searches for sources.

subsystems.name: Low-background geoneutrino detection
subsystems.role: measures antineutrinos from uranium and thorium decay inside the Earth.
parts: inverse-beta-decay detection of positron plus neutron

buildSteps.title: Pick the site
buildSteps.detail: Either a cubic kilometre of very clear natural ice or water, or a deep underground cavern where rock shields out cosmic rays — as in the existing neutrino detectors.

buildSteps.title: Drill or excavate
buildSteps.detail: For ice arrays, a hot-water drill melts holes roughly 2.5 km deep; for water arrays, sensors are attached to mooring strings and lowered; for tank detectors, a cavity is excavated and lined.

buildSteps.title: Deploy the sensors
buildSteps.detail: Photomultipliers in pressure housings are lowered on strings and frozen in place or suspended, spaced tens of metres apart to give the array its resolution.

buildSteps.title: Connect power and data
buildSteps.detail: Each string carries cables to a surface or shore station that supplies power and streams the digitised hits.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the array
buildSteps.detail: Pulsed light sources at known positions are flashed to measure timing offsets, sensor efficiency and the optical properties of the medium.

buildSteps.title: Commission and filter
buildSteps.detail: The detector runs, a fast trigger throws away most cosmic-ray muons, and surviving events are transmitted for offline analysis.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct events
buildSteps.detail: Software fits the pattern of photon arrival times to recover a direction and energy; a through-going muon track, for example, traces back toward its source.

buildSteps.title: Search for sources
buildSteps.detail: Sky maps are built from many events to look for point sources, the diffuse Galactic flux, or a burst from a supernova.

buildSteps.title: For planetary work
buildSteps.detail: A sufficiently large, low-background detector counts geoneutrinos; the count and spectrum constrain how much radiogenic heat the crust and mantle produce.

prerequisites.tech: Large photomultiplier tubes and rugged pressure housings
prerequisites.why: without cheap, reliable light sensors a kilometre-scale array is unaffordable.

prerequisites.tech: Deep drilling and subsea mooring technology
prerequisites.why: sensors must survive years at kilometres of depth without maintenance.

prerequisites.tech: Nanosecond timing and high-bandwidth data acquisition
prerequisites.why: direction is inferred almost entirely from the relative arrival times of photons.
the muon rate at shallow depth is millions of times the neutrino rate.
geoneutrino counting needs detectors whose own radioactivity is far below the signal.
turning a geoneutrino count into an actual image of the Earth's interior requires directionality no current detector has.

pathway.milestone: operating kilometre-scale arrays (IceCube, Baikal-GVD, KM3NeT under construction) plus underground water and scintillator detectors
pathway.unlocks: neutrino maps of the sky and the first multi-messenger astronomy with neutrinos.

pathway.milestone: planned enlargements such as IceCube-Gen2 and completion of KM3NeT
pathway.unlocks: enough events to resolve individual sources rather than just a diffuse glow.

pathway.milestone: larger low-background detectors measuring geoneutrinos from crust and mantle
pathway.unlocks: independent constraints on how much of Earth's internal heat comes from radioactive decay.

pathway.milestone: directional antineutrino or atmospheric-neutrino radiography of a whole planet
pathway.unlocks: true tomography of Earth's deep interior, and eventually of other planetary bodies.
